nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Drinking water standards and regulations|Contaminant level limits_qna_000
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What range of indoor radon concentrations was observed in the studies?
nodes.answer: The minimum concentration measured was 14.3 Bq/m3 and the maximum was 1083 Bq/m3.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Drinking water standards and regulations|Contaminant level limits_qna_001
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: How is the threshold defined in the context of the study?
nodes.answer: The threshold is defined as the 99th percentile of the data.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Drinking water standards and regulations|Contaminant level limits_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How did the concentration of DEET affect the biochemical composition of Chlorella vulgaris?
nodes.answer: When DEET concentration exceeded the tolerance limit of 17.4 mg/L, the pigments and biochemical concentrations in Chlorella vulgaris drastically reduced, indicating irreversible damage.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Drinking water standards and regulations|Contaminant level limits_qna_003
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Which heavy metals were found at concentrations exceeding recommended levels in the ICUW?
nodes.answer: Heavy metals exceeding recommended levels included arsenic, boron, bromide, fluoride, and nitrate.
